To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RCL expressed by P. pastoris is N-glycoslated and that the glycosylation of N-14 and especially N-60 plays a role in the expression of RCL.
RCL expressed by P. pastoris was N-linked glycosylated at N-14, -48 and -60, and the glycosylation of N-60 played an important role in RCL expression, secretion and thermostability.
RCL is N-glycoslyated at the sites of N-14, and N-60, and N-glycosylyation on the site N-60 is essential for the expression of RCL in the methylotrophic yeast P. pastoris.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of N-linked glycan on the secretion and enzymic properties of RCL expressed in a methylotrophic yeast Pichia pastorisis.
the N-glycosite of RCL and the role of N-linked glycoforms in the protein expression and activity.
the glycosylation of RCL in the yeast P. pastoris and the role of the N-glycose in the secretion and properties of RCL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-linked glycan on N60 is the main contributor to the secretion and activity, while the N-linked glycans on N14 and N48 have no obvious effect on the secretion and catalytic activity of RCL.
N-linked glycosylations on different sites of the RCL protein have different effects on the protein secretion and enzymatic activities.
the N-linked glycan on the different sites has a specific effect on the secretion and enzymatically properties of RCL in the yeast expression system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-glycosites of RCL were N-glycoslated, and the N-glycations on the different sites of RCL had different functions for RCL expression and enzymatic properties in P. pastorisa.
the glycan of N-60 plays a key role in RCL secretion and the glycan on N14 is beneficial for the catalytic activity of RCL.
the N-glycosites of RCL were not only the sites for the N-linked glycan modification but also the sites that could be modified by the glycosyltransferases to regulate the secretion and activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-glycanylation of the lipase on the N-14 and -60 site can be beneficial for the expression and stability of the enzyme.
the modification of N-glycosites in RCL can be used to improve its expression level and thermostability, which may have potential application in industry.
the N-glycosite on N-60 is a key site for RCL secretion, while the N-glycose on N-14 is a key site that affects the catalytic activity of the lipase.
